p.src: Overview: A law of motion must do more than relate familiar physical quantities. It must specify the state of a system, carry that state from one instant to the next, and reveal which distinctions and quantities survive the motion. We shall reach Newtonian mechanics by first testing a plausible but wrong force law, then enlarge the state from position to phase space, and finally derive conservation of momentum and energy.

We shall reach Newtonian mechanics by first testing a plausible but wrong force law, then enlarge the state from position to phase space, and finally derive conservation of momentum and energy.
ja: 概観: 運動法則は、なじみ深い物理量を関係づけるだけでは不十分である。系の状態を指定し、その状態をある瞬間から次の瞬間へ運び、運動を経てもなお生き残る区別と量を示さなければならない。まずもっともらしいが誤った力の法則を検証し、次に状態を位置から位相空間へ拡大し、最後に運動量とエネルギーの保存を導くことによって、ニュートン力学に到達する。
zh: 概述: 运动定律不能仅仅把熟悉的物理量联系起来。它必须指定系统的状态，把该状态从一个时刻带到下一个时刻，并揭示哪些区分和哪些量在运动中得以保留。我们将先检验一条看似合理但错误的力定律，然后把状态从位置扩展到相空间，最后导出动量守恒和能量守恒，由此到达牛顿力学。

p.src: Everyday motion is dominated by friction. Push a heavy object across a floor and it moves; stop pushing and it soon stops. A larger push generally produces a larger speed, while a heavier object requires a harder push. In such a world, it is natural to suppose that force produces velocity itself. This was the basic intuition behind the Aristotelian description of motion.

ja: 日常の運動は摩擦に支配されている。重い物体を床の上で押せば動き、押すのをやめればまもなく止まる。より大きな力で押せば一般により大きな速さが生じ、より重い物体にはより強い押しが必要である。そのような世界では、力が速度そのものを生み出すと考えるのは自然である。これがアリストテレス的な運動記述の背後にあった基本的な直観であった。
zh: 日常运动由摩擦主导。把一个重物在地板上推一下，它就会移动；停止推，它很快就停下来。推得越用力，速度通常越大；而越重的物体需要越大的推力。在这样的世界里，人们自然会设想力本身产生速度。这就是亚里士多德对运动的描述背后的基本直觉。

p.src: Ice skating supplies the missing experience. A skater needs force to start, stop, or change direction, but not to continue gliding once in motion. Had Aristotle worked on nearly frictionless ice rather than ordinary ground, the defect in the force–velocity intuition would have been much harder to miss.

p.src: The future is easy to predict: every initial displacement approaches the same resting configuration. The past is another matter. Suppose the particle is observed very near the origin with only finite accuracy. The law is therefore suspicious from the standpoint of reversible fundamental dynamics.

p.src: This does not mean that Aristotle was irrational. The friction-dominated motion he described really is dissipative. The mistake was to promote that effective behavior to a fundamental law. Friction is itself a force arising from complicated microscopic interactions. When a hand pushes an object at roughly steady speed, the applied force is balancing friction; the applied force is not creating velocity as such.

p.src: The second circularity concerns force and mass. If force is defined as mass times acceleration and mass as force divided by acceleration, the equation seems empty. An operational experiment separates the definitions from the law. Compare an object with a standard kilogram by balancing the two, then attach the object to a spring balance in otherwise force-free space. Define one unit of force by a fixed small extension of the spring. Two identical springs, each stretched by that same amount, provide two units of force and produce twice the acceleration. It is safer to add a second spring than to stretch one spring twice as far, because a real spring eventually becomes nonlinear or breaks. Keeping one spring but joining two equal masses produces half the acceleration; three equal masses produce one third.

ja: 回答: それは定義によって保証されるのではなく、検証されるものである。成功した法則を調べ、共通する実験的特徴を特定し、それらの特徴を原理へと高める。より深い論理的順序は逆方向に走る。量子場の理論の方がより基本的であり、ニュートン力学は低速運動や重い物体といった近似を通じて現れる。講義はより単純な法則から積み上げなければならないので、可逆性は今、その到達範囲が後に検証される原理として導入される。
